/-!
# Erdős Problem 502

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/502](https://www.erdosproblems.com/502)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [BBS83] Bannai, Eiichi and Bannai, Etsuko and Stanton, Dennis, *An upper bound for the
  cardinality of an $s$-distance subset in real Euclidean space. II*. Combinatorica (1983),
  147-152.
- [PePo21] Petrov, Fedor and Pohoata, Cosmin, *A remark on sets with few distances in
  $\mathbb{R}^d$*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2021), 569-571.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos502

/--
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ such that there are only two distinct
distances between elements of $A$? That is,
$$\# \{ \lvert x-y\rvert : x\neq y\in A\} = 2.$$

Asked to Erdős by Coxeter. Bannai, Bannai, and Stanton [BBS83] have proved that
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \binom{n+2}{2}.$$
A simple proof of this upper bound was given by Petrov and Pohoata [PePo21].

The exact maximum is not known in general: a lower bound of $\binom{n+1}{2}$ follows from the
construction of Alweiss (see [503]). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos502.lean"]
theorem erdos_502 (n : ℕ) (A : Set (ℝ^n)) (hA : A.Finite)
    (hA2 : {d : ℝ | ∃ x ∈ A, ∃ y ∈ A, x ≠ y ∧ dist x y = d}.ncard = 2) :
    A.ncard ≤ (n + 2).choose 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos502

Petrov and Pohoata, A remark on sets with few distances in R^d, arXiv:1912.08181v1, introduction and Theorem 1.1; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1912.08181
Crossref publisher-deposited record for Petrov–Pohoata, DOI 10.1090/proc/15231 (abstract, publication details, and bibliography).

Independent Erdős problem database, entry 502 (status corroboration): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md
review.notes:
Erdos502.erdos_502 faithfully states the cited Bannai–Bannai–Stanton upper bound, explicitly identified in its docstring; it does not assert an exact maximum. Petrov–Pohoata's Theorem 1.1 specializes directly to this statement at s = 2. The research solved category is appropriate for that bound.

Checked the Euclidean metric, finiteness and ncard conventions, exclusion of zero distances, quantifiers, and binomial coefficient. Scratch proofs confirm the empty/singleton and dimension-zero cases are harmless and exhibit three points in R^1 with exactly two distances. All statement-check experiments compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

Access limitations: erdosproblems.com/502, its discussion page, and /503 returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the claim was verified against accessible primary literature instead. The linked formal proof states a general theorem implying the reviewed declaration and contains no textual proof gaps or custom axioms. Its exact Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 environment was unavailable, so its kernel proof was not independently revalidated; compilation under the available 4.33.1 encountered version-dependent errors, which are not evidence of a defect in the original proof.
